exit_polls.methodology: In 2026 the network exit poll became 'The Voter Poll' by SSRS, shared by CNN, ABC, AP, CBS, Fox News, MS NOW and NBC (CNN: ~100,000 voters incl. ~22,000 Election Day in-person interviews in 15 states; Fox/AP: ~80,000 registered voters, all 50 states, Oct 19-Nov 3, MoE +/-0.6). So 'CNN/Edison', 'AP VoteCast' and 'Fox Voter Analysis' are no longer separate surveys; group numbers are identical across outlets. Page re-checked 11:07 AM ET Nov 4; all rows unchanged. Page shows no 2022 or per-group 2024 comparisons. margin_2024 values (where filled) are Harris minus Trump from NBC's 2024 presidential exit poll page (Edison/NEP national exit poll, the vintage currently displayed), a different survey and method than the 2026 SSRS Voter Poll, and a presidential (not House) vote; AP VoteCast 2024 figures differ (e.g., AP says under-30 were 'roughly split' in 2024 vs Harris +11 in the NBC exit poll). Area-type 2024 margins omitted because 2024 exit poll urban/suburban shares (29/52) imply a different definition than 2026 (20/45). The AP fieldwork was Oct 19-Nov 3 in Alaska and Oct 22-Nov 3 elsewhere (PBS/AP).

nyt_voter_trends_secondhand.claim: No secondhand coverage of the NYT 'How Americans Voted in 2026' voter-trends interactive (or its state pages) was found via search of news outlets, aggregators or social posts as of ~11 AM ET Nov 4. Its findings are captured first-hand from a user-supplied PDF in research/nyt_voter_trends.json (House D 56-43, shift +15 vs 2024 presidential; 18-29 +32 shift; Hispanic +28; non-college +17 vs college +11).
Yahoo News recap cites NYT projections that, as of 1 a.m. ET Wednesday, Democrats were projected to gain more than three dozen House seats (NYT projections, not the voter-trends page).

Pre-election (Sept 2026): Nate Cohn's NYT analysis, per secondary coverage, found high-quality polls had Democrats ahead 64-29 among Hispanic likely voters on the generic ballot vs Harris +7 in final 2024 surveys.

notes: Key structural fact: in 2026 the separate exit polls were replaced by a single SSRS 'Voter Poll' shared by CNN, ABC, AP, CBS, Fox, MS NOW and NBC, so CNN/NBC/Fox/ABC/AP group numbers are the same survey; there is no separate Edison exit poll, AP VoteCast (NORC) or Fox Voter Analysis to compare. CNN pages returned HTTP 451 (blocked), so CNN-specific text, 2022 group comparisons and CNN's crosstab page could not be read. CBS exit-poll tables are images. None of the fetched Voter Poll pages report per-group 2024 or 2022 margins, so margin_2024/margin_2022 are null except where a secondary source gave both party shares (Latino 2024 via NBC article; young white and young rural via CIRCLE/AP VoteCast 2024). The overall Voter Poll House topline (D% vs R%) was not displayed on the fetched pages. No running official national House popular-vote tally with share counted was found; popular-vote margin relies on G. Elliott Morris's estimate (method undisclosed) and the NYT model (user PDF). Shift computations vs 2024 are this researcher's arithmetic. House and Senate counts are snapshots ~10:40-10:55 AM ET Nov 4 and will change; NBC called-seat numbers and AP numbers (via Al Jazeera) differ due to timing. The NBC 2024 exit poll page (fetched at verification) does show men Trump 55, Harris 43; 2024 margins for core groups were added from that page during verification. The 2022 turnout rate (46.8%) was confirmed on the fetched Ballotpedia page, citing the US Elections Project.
